To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TPTAM radical can be used as a pHe reporter to measure pHe in tumors in vivo.
a triphosphono trityl radical is an effective EPR pH reporter for in vivo extracellular pH measurement.
a triphosphonic acid triarylmethyl radical is an excellent pH‐responsive pHe EPR probe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization, and evaluation of the TPTAM as a pHe molecular reporter.
the development of new molecular probes for EPR‐pHmetry.
the development and application of a new method of measuring the extracellular pH in vivo using EPR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the TPTAM radical is a reliable and robust method for pHe measurement in vivo.
the pHe values measured in vivo by EPR using the triphosphonate‐TPTAM probe are in the range of 7.0–7.4.

the use of TPTAM as a pHe reporter in vivo is a feasible approach, but further improvements in the TPTAM design, in the dosing regimen, in the EPR instrumentation and in the data acquisition protocol are necessary to achieve a better pHe resolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TPTAM is a promising pH‐sensitive reporter for EPR extracellular pHe measurements in tumors.
the TPTAM‐based EPR pH‐sensor is a promising tool for in vivo pHe monitoring in tumors and that it can be further improved by optimizing its chemical structure.
the TPTAM radical is a promising pHe reporter for EPR‐pHe‐metry in vivo, with the potential to be further improved for clinical applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pHe of tumors can be measured in vivo by EPR using the TPTAM reporter.
TPTAM is a suitable pHe reporter for in vivo EPR measurements in mice bearing tumors with different pHe, and that it can also be used for in vitro measurements in cell cultures.
TPTAM is a promising pH‐sensitive EPR reporter for pHe imaging in tumors.
